coverage_intent: Distinct-human evidence must be stronger than distinct keys, credentials or issuer records.
Semantic claims remain proof-system agnostic across implementations.
Suite identification is deterministic and prevents cross-suite ambiguity.
Negotiation is transcript-bound and downgrade resistant.
Deprecation, overlap, rollback and migration preserve semantic meaning.
Material setup, hardware, prover and registry dependencies are disclosed.
Security and privacy claims are bounded by an explicit assurance horizon.
Post-quantum migration triggers, overlap and downgrade protections are testable.
Lineage mechanisms do not over-claim restoration of broken cryptographic guarantees.
Epoch rollover, overlap and deletion bound intentionally linkable state.
Long-lived roots, keys and parameters have cryptoperiods and rotation triggers.
Retention has purpose, access, expiry and deletion/archive semantics without extending proof assurance.
Status cadence, cache age, effective-time and unavailable-state behaviour are deterministic.
Material claims define events and times that force re-evaluation or downgrade.
Historical evidence distinguishes valid-as-of evaluation from current validity.
